cards.headline: Two scientists awarded 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for discoveries regarding mirror-image molecules

pages.text: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announced in Stockholm, Sweden, on Wednesday that the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry has been awarded to Henri B Kagan of Paris-Sud University in France and Kensō Soai of Tokyo University of Science in Japan. The scientists received the prize for the discovery of nonlinear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis, which demonstrated how chemical reactions can produce an overwhelming excess of one of two mirror-image forms of a molecule. The two recipients will each receive an equal share of a 12 million Swedish kronor prize, valued at approximately £900,000. This property, known as chirality, allows molecules to exist in two forms that contain the same atoms but act as mirror images of one another. While laboratory reactions typically produce equal quantities of both forms, the chemistry underpinning life is homochiral, meaning it is same-handed; for example, proteins are built almost exclusively from L-amino acids. Prof Andre Cobb, an organic chemist at King’s College London, noted that because many molecules in the body are chiral, the different versions of a drug can interact with the body in different ways, potentially leading to weakened or different drug effects. The drug thalidomide was cited as a potent example of these differing interactions.

cards.headline: ECNEC approves 13 projects in Bangladesh totaling Tk 162 billion

pages.text: The Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) approved 13 projects involving a total cost of Tk 162 billion on October 7, 2026. The approval occurred during the committee's fifth meeting at the Bangladesh Secretariat, chaired by Prime Minister and ECNEC Chairman Tarique Rahman. Of the 13 projects, 10 are new, two are revised, and one involves an extension of an implementation period. State Minister for Planning Zonayed Abdur Rahim Saki briefed reporters following the meeting. The total funding for the approved projects includes Tk 106 billion from government funds, Tk 40.8 billion from project loans, and Tk 15.2 billion from the funds of concerned agencies. One of the approved projects is a Tk 24.9 billion plan to construct a 442-megawatt peak (MWp) solar power plant at Rampal in Bagerhat.

The Rampal solar power plant project, proposed by the Power Division and to be implemented by the Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB), aims to increase renewable energy generation, diversify primary fuel sources, and reduce carbon emissions. The Planning Commission recommended implementation from September 2026 to March 2029. The plant will be built on 918.50 acres of land in Block-B of Rampal, which the BPDB previously acquired in 2012 for a coal-fired power plant. The Planning Commission stated that using this existing land would eliminate the need for fresh land acquisition and reduce costs. The project will be financed by the BPDB using Tk 3.74 billion from its own funds and Tk 21.23 billion from the Power Sector Development Fund. The latter loan carries a 2 per cent interest rate with a one-year grace period and a 16-year repayment period. Once implemented, the plant is expected to add 442 MW of electricity to the national grid and utilize existing transmission infrastructure from the nearby Rampal coal-fired power plant. The Planning Commission noted the project would support the government's target of reaching a 20 per cent renewable energy share in the total energy mix by 2030. Currently, solar power generation in the country stands at 797 MW out of a total on-grid capacity of 28,827 MW.

cards.headline: Bangladesh Bank allows foreign currency accounts for approved foreign loan proceeds

pages.text: Bangladesh Bank (BB) has authorized designated authorized dealer (AD) banks to open and maintain foreign currency (FC) accounts for eligible private sector industrial borrowers to hold proceeds from approved foreign loans. According to a report by BSS, the central bank issued this instruction on a Wednesday to facilitate the cross-border settlement of payments related to these loans. Under the circular, private sector industrial enterprises in Bangladesh may access medium- and long-term external financing provided they receive prior approval from competent authorities. Authorized dealer banks are required to obtain and retain copies of specific approvals, such as those from the Scrutiny Committee on Foreign Loan or Supplier's Credit of the Invest Bangladesh Authority, or from the Standing Committee on Non-Concessional Loan (SCNCL) and Bangladesh Bank where applicable.

Balances held in these FC accounts may be used for import payments following prevailing Import Policy Orders and foreign exchange regulations, as well as for bona fide service payments necessary for project implementation. For service payments, banks must conduct due diligence, including the deduction and payment of applicable taxes and VAT, and obtain competent authority approval where required. The circular also permits the encashment of foreign currency into Taka from these accounts for local procurement, subject to relevant approval provisions. These accounts may earn interest or profit based on the terms of the banker-customer relationship. Authorized dealer banks must report the utilization of loan proceeds to the Foreign Exchange Investment Department (FEID) of Bangladesh Bank on a quarterly basis, covering the quarters ending in December, March, June, and September. Once the drawdown and utilization of the loan proceeds are complete, the accounts must be closed and the FEID informed, though accounts may be maintained until maturity if the loan agreement requires fund retention for repayment.

cards.headline: EU negotiators travel to China to discuss curbing hybrid electric car imports

pages.text: EU trade negotiators are traveling to China for two days of talks aimed at reaching a deal to curb the export of cheap hybrid electric cars into Europe. The negotiations, led by Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič and his team, are scheduled to begin on Thursday and continue through October 2, 2026. Negotiators are reportedly seeking a “proof of concept” pilot agreement in the automotive sector that could potentially be scaled to other industries in future months. The effort seeks to address Beijing’s trade surplus, which has reached £1bn a day, and aims to achieve “tangible, meaningful and measurable” results ahead of an EU leaders' meeting in Brussels on October 1, 2026, where China is a high-priority agenda item. Sources indicate the mood in the talks has shifted as EU member states have increased demands for protection against Chinese imports that threaten domestic industries.

Diplomatic efforts to prevent a full-scale trade war began in late June. Last month, the EU requested that China voluntarily restrict hybrid exports to address rising sales, warning that failure to do so could result in safeguards, such as quotas. Following the imposition of EU tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles in October 2024, there was an increase in the export of hybrid cars, which were not subject to those tariffs. While the EU has sought these restrictions, China's specific response to the request for voluntary limits is not known. Sources have noted historical difficulty in curbing Chinese exports to the EU due to the country's ability to pivot quickly when trade barriers are implemented.

According to the President, more than 1,000 people have been supported to own homes through interventions involving the Fund and partner financial institutions. Figures presented at the conference indicated that Ghana has a housing deficit of 1.8 million units.

Addressing the housing challenge, President Mahama stated that the issue involves both the availability of houses and the ability of households to secure affordable financing. He noted that self-employed workers, such as traders, artisans, farmers, and transport operators, often face difficulties securing mortgages because they may lack the payslips or conventional banking records required by providers. cards.headline: Parti Québécois wins election in Quebec, Canada

pages.text: The Parti Québécois (PQ) won the Quebec provincial election on October 5, 2026, gaining its first power in 14 years. Led by Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, the party added 56 seats to its roster and more than doubled its vote share compared to the 2022 election. Despite the victory, the PQ fell five seats short of a majority and secured approximately 28% of the popular vote, which polling analyst Philippe Fournier identified as the lowest percentage for any government in Canadian electoral history. This lack of a majority complicates the party's promise to hold a referendum on separating the French-speaking province from Canada after Donald Trump leaves office in 2028. On October 6, 2026, Plamondon announced he would prevent the lieutenant governor, who represents the British crown, from swearing in his new government.

The election results reflect a province where the vast majority of voters chose parties that do not seek a referendum. According to reports from The Guardian World and CBC Canada, the PQ faces several challenges, including opposition to plans to reduce immigration levels from the business community and farmers, and initiatives to apply strict language laws to colleges and abolish the monarchy. While Plamondon pledged in his victory speech to be a “good-faith collaborator” with the rest of the country, the province's most popular politician remains Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, largely due to his resistance to Donald Trump. The PQ's rise follows the fall of the incumbent Coalition Avenir Québec.

The Palestinian Central Elections Commission was prevented from entering both territories on Tuesday to oversee preparations, the official Palestinian WAFA news agency reported, citing a Palestinian official. Although the commission stated last week that preparations remained on track despite Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas extending the candidate nomination period from 12 to 18 days, Jibril Rajoub, a senior official in Abbas’ Fatah movement, stated last month that he did not expect the legislative election to take place on schedule. Rajoub suggested holding a presidential election first to address part of the problem. President Abbas was elected in 2005 for a term that expired in 2009, and no presidential election has occurred since.

cards.headline: WHO assesses low epidemic risk in Russia following death of lab technician in Siberia

pages.text: The World Health Organization (WHO) stated on October 6, 2026, that the risk of an epidemic in Russia is low following the death of Darya Shipilova, a 28-year-old lab technician at a plague research institute in Irkutsk, Siberia. WHO spokesperson Christian Lindmeier said on October 6, 2026, that there have been no signs of a wider outbreak and that all identified contacts of the patient are being monitored, with none showing symptoms to date. The WHO assessed the health risk as moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for the rest of Russia, and very low for Europe. Russian officials are investigating whether viral pneumonic plague caused the death, though authorities have stated Shipilova died of “pneumonia of an unknown aetiology.” Russian media reports suggested she may have become infected following an accident at her workplace, where dangerous pathogens are studied. Shipilova died last week, two days after falling ill. Since October 2, 2026, Russian media has reported that 60 of Shipilova’s colleagues have been locked in the institute, sleeping on floors and chairs while tests are conducted. Strict quarantine measures have also been imposed at five neighboring hospitals, where relatives are forbidden from seeing patients. WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus urged Russia on October 6, 2026, to be transparent regarding the death, stating on X that timely and complete information sharing is essential to clarify conflicting reports and assess public health risks.

cards.headline: Human Rights Watch reports ongoing assault on civil and political rights in Bangladesh

pages.text: Human Rights Watch (HRW) has reported that the mass arrest of attendees at a small left-wing party’s meeting in Dhaka is the latest incident in an ongoing assault on civil and political rights by Bangladesh authorities. On 26 September, police took approximately 290 supporters of the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal into custody after members of the Jubo Dal—the youth wing of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP)—claimed the gathering was a secret meeting of the banned Awami League, the party of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina. A court remanded 27 of those arrested to custody following allegations they chanted 'Joy Bangla,' a slogan associated with the Awami League. The Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal was previously part of a 14-party alliance led by the Awami League that governed Bangladesh from 2009 until 2024. The Awami League was toppled by student-led protests in which security forces killed hundreds of people.

According to the HRW report, the BNP has targeted perceived opponents with arbitrary detention since being elected in February, leaving hundreds of Awami League members in jail, mostly without charge. On 26 September, police in Barisal detained 12 Awami League activists for allegedly holding a secret meeting to plan sabotage; two days later, 15 people were arrested in Dhaka under the Anti-Terrorism Act on similar allegations. Those detained stated they had gathered to mark the birthday of Sheikh Hasina. HRW noted that while the Awami League government was characterized by grave rights violations, including extrajudicial killings and enforced disappearances, the current BNP government has instead arbitrarily detained opponents and rolled back human rights safeguards proposed by the interim government.

pages.text: A 145-year-old heritage home near Kensington Market in Toronto, Canada, may face demolition following its purchase earlier this year by the utility company Hydro One. cards.headline: Yemen's internationally recognized government launches military operation to retake Houthi-held areas

pages.text: On October 4, 2026, Yemen’s Saudi-backed, internationally recognized government launched a major military operation aimed at retaking areas controlled by the Houthis. Rashad al-Alimi, President of the Yemeni Presidential Leadership Council, stated in a televised address that government forces would continue operations until Houthi control is ended. Al-Alimi noted the decision to launch the offensive followed the exhaustion of efforts to reduce tensions and called on regional and international partners to support the council's institutions. The offensive follows recent Houthi gains in strategic highlands near Taiz, which brought the group closer to the last road linking Taiz with the government seat in Aden. According to the AFP news agency, more than 70 people were reportedly killed in fighting around Taiz over the past day. The Yemeni military reported that operations were commencing in the Houthi-held capital, Sanaa, while allied forces reportedly retook the town of Dhubab north of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Simultaneously, the Saudi-led coalition reported hitting Houthi military targets in Hodeida on the Red Sea coast, with a coalition spokesman stating naval forces destroyed weapons depots, facilities for booby-trapped boats and naval mines, and thwarted a planned attack on southern Red Sea waterways.

The escalation included retaliatory strikes from the Houthis. A Houthi military spokesman stated the group launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco facilities in Riyadh and the Khurais area, as well as King Khalid International Airport and an oil refinery in the Red Sea city of Rabigh. The Houthis claimed these attacks were in response to approximately 50 air and missile strikes carried out by the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen over the previous 12 hours. cards.headline: Bangladesh and World Bank sign $300 million deal for food security project

pages.text: The Government of Bangladesh and the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank Group signed a financing agreement on Monday to implement the “Emergency Support for Food Security Project.” The agreement is for 219,200,000.00 Special Drawing Rights (SDR), equivalent to $300.00 million. According to an Economic Relations Division (ERD) press release, the project aims to support food security by ensuring the availability of eligible fertilisers, specifically for smallholder farmers, during planting seasons. The project's implementation period is scheduled from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027. The agreement was signed by Shahriar Kader Siddiky, Secretary of the Economic Relations Division (ERD) within the Ministry of Finance, and Jean Pesme, the World Bank Division Director for Bangladesh and Bhutan.

The project will be carried out by the Finance Division (FD) in coordination with the Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation (BCIC) and the Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC). The loan includes a 25-year maturity period, which incorporates a five-year grace period. It carries an interest rate of 1.5% per annum on the Withdrawn Credit Balance and a maximum commitment fee of up to 0.50% per annum on the Unwithdrawn Financing Balance. The World Bank has waived the commitment fee for Bangladesh for several years, including the current fiscal year.

cards.headline: Advance voting for Toronto’s 2026 municipal election begins September 29

pages.text: Advance voting for the 2026 municipal election in Toronto, Canada, is scheduled to begin on September 29, 2026. According to the City of Toronto, advance voting will take place from September 29 to October 6, and from October 4 to October 11, between the hours of 10 a.m. and 7 p.m. The city is offering two voting locations in each of its 25 wards, and eligible voters may choose to vote at either location within their specific ward. Advance voting turnout data is scheduled to be released in a news release on October 13, following the Monday, October 12 holiday.

Packages can be returned via 25 secure, yellow Toronto Elections drop boxes located throughout the city, with one box situated in each ward. cards.headline: Poll shows Alberta NDP gaining ground amid UCP independence referendum

pages.text: A CBC News poll of 1,200 Albertans suggests the United Conservative Party (UCP) is now essentially neck-and-neck with the opposition New Democratic Party (NDP), following a decline in personal impressions of Premier Danielle Smith and support for her governing party. In battleground Calgary, the NDP leads by eight points. Calgary-based pollster Janet Brown noted that the referendum asking if Alberta should remain a province of Canada may have provided the NDP with increased capacity and a chance to organize their ground game a year ahead of a general election. Brown stated that the UCP usually maintains a superior ground game for mobilizing voters. An Alberta political watcher suggested that Premier Smith may have triggered the Oct. 19 referendum to demonstrate a commitment to direct democracy to her party's base, but that the move may have unintentionally strengthened the NDP. NDP president Heth Wilson said the referendum has attracted people from across the province who want to get involved.

The shifting political landscape follows a September byelection in the Calgary-Shaw constituency, a riding with a long history of electing conservative politicians. In that election, NDP candidate Kyle Campbell defeated the UCP's Mike Derry by nearly 600 votes. cards.headline: Iran’s oil minister resigns amid economic crisis and allegations of missing oil revenues

pages.text: Mohsen Paknejad, Iran’s oil minister, has resigned, with President Masoud Pezeshkian stating that Paknejad cited personal reasons for his departure. According to reporting by The Guardian World, the resignation follows allegations from the Farhikhtegan newspaper that an intermediary trust established during Paknejad’s tenure owes the state-owned National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) nearly $2bn (£1.5bn) in export revenues. The report further alleged that three individual trustees awarded oil contracts allegedly owe hundreds of millions of dollars each to the NIOC. Iran has utilized informal networks known as “trustees” to bypass US sanctions and repatriate oil revenues.

The resignation occurs as Iran faces a significant economic contraction and inflation of 85%. The country's economy contracted by 10% during the first three months of the year. A drop in oil receipts has resulted in a shortfall in foreign exchange earnings and one of the largest declines in the value of the rial since the 1979 Iranian revolution; the rial has traded more than 10% lower than a month ago. This currency decline is attributed largely to a US naval blockade preventing the sale of oil. While the central bank stated its role is to manage fluctuations rather than defend a specific rate, emergency government meetings held over the weekend reportedly yielded little tangible progress. Additionally, reports indicate that members of the professional middle class, including nurses and teachers, are resigning in large numbers due to salaries failing to keep pace with price increases. Regarding international relations, Iranian diplomats are reportedly not planning new concessions following the rejection of a proposal to accelerate nuclear negotiations by Donald Trump one week ago.

cards.headline: UAE prosecutor says Flydubai co-pilot used crash axe in attempted terrorist attack

pages.text: United Arab Emirates prosecutor general Hamad Saif al-Shamsi stated that the co-pilot of Flydubai flight FZ1073 attempted to carry out a “terrorist attack” using a crash axe. The incident occurred on September 30, 2026, during an Israel-bound flight carrying 182 people. According to Al-Shamsi, the axe is an implement typically kept inside the cockpit for emergencies, such as fires or crashes, and would not have required covert smuggling. The aircraft plunged 16,625ft in just over 30 seconds during the event, a descent so extreme that part of the rudder was ripped off. A disaster was narrowly averted when passengers and crew intervened to stop the co-pilot's attempt to take control of the plane. The Flydubai captain, identified as Indian national Smit Machchhar, reported that he used his remaining energy to unlock the cockpit door, allowing others to enter, subdue the co-pilot, and stabilize the aircraft. Machchhar sustained wounds to his head, hands, and neck. Both the captain and co-pilot were taken to the UAE for medical treatment following immediate care in Saudi Arabia.

Media outlets have identified the co-pilot as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national. Reports from the Wall Street Journal and the Associated Press indicate that al-Hammami had previously been barred from flying by Oman due to concerns regarding extremist views, after which he was moved to an administrative role at Oman Air before being hired by Flydubai. It remains unclear to what extent he was vetted during the hiring process. Investigations are ongoing to determine if al-Hammami acted as a “lone wolf” or had connections to extremist groups. On October 2, 2026, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that the co-pilot had undergone “Islamist radicalization,” though he provided no evidence. Security agencies from four regional countries, including Israel, are working to establish motives with assistance from the United States and other Western governments. cards.headline: US Air Force redeploys bombers from RAF Fairford in England following suspected terror attack investigation

pages.text: The US Air Force has redeployed all bombers stationed at RAF Fairford, a US-run military air base in England, back to their home stations in the United States. According to a Pentagon official speaking on condition of anonymity on October 4, 2026, the movement follows an investigation into a planned terror attack at the base. A Pentagon spokesperson acknowledged the redeployment, noting that operational security precluded real-time confirmation of asset movements. Aviation observers, including the Military Air Tracking Alliance, had previously noted dozens of B-52 and B-1 bombers operating out of the Gloucestershire base since the start of the Iran war. On October 4, 2026, observers noted at least 10 of 12 B-1 bombers flying out of the base, including some that had arrived on rotation less than a week prior. This rapid departure follows a security incident at RAF Fairford in late September and the subsequent arrest of a dual British-Iranian national in central London on suspicion of plotting a terror attack. In total, six people have been taken into custody and released on bail during the investigation. British authorities have linked the incident to Tehran, though Iran has denied involvement.

The withdrawal occurs as President Donald Trump weighs options regarding the war in Iran. On October 3, 2026, while leaving the White House for a rally in Ohio, Trump told reporters, “We have decisions that I’ll make about Iran. Iran’s been decimated. So the only question is — it’ll either be the easy way, or the hard way.” RAF Fairford, located 100 miles west of London, has been used by American bombers for decades during Middle East conflicts. While the UK Ministry of Defence provided no immediate comment, reporting suggests the withdrawal appears to be a response to security concerns regarding the safety of the base.

pages.text: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated on Sunday that the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until seven conditions, outlined in an interim understanding reached with the United States last June, are fulfilled. Ghalibaf, speaking via the state-linked news agency Nournews, said the decision follows Tehran receiving a U.S. response to its diplomatic proposal. Ghalibaf stated that Tehran would no longer accept stalling or the imposition of unilateral demands, asserting that the resumption of navigation through the strait is tied to the fulfillment of conditions based on the Islamabad memorandum of understanding. He added that Iran would both fight and negotiate and is prepared to confront the U.S. with new surprises on the military battlefield. Last week, U.S. President Donald Trump ruled out an Iranian proposal to reopen the strait, which is used to ship one-fifth of global oil and natural gas during peacetime.

pages.text: In Latvia's parliamentary election, the centrist United List party led by Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs secured a historic victory, appearing to win the largest share of votes since the country regained independence from the Soviet Union in 1991. Preliminary results indicated that with 97% to 99.9% of ballots counted, the United List earned approximately 35.3% to 35.4% of the vote, granting the party 42 of the 100 seats in the Saeima. The result places Kulbergs, a 47-year-old businessman and amateur rally driver, in a position to form a pro-Ukraine coalition. Kulbergs, who assumed office in May after a previous coalition collapsed following incidents involving stray Ukrainian military drones, stated on the night of October 3, 2026, that he would not cooperate with pro-Russian parties and specifically ruled out a coalition with the populist Latvia First party. Political scientist Roberts Kits noted that the United List could potentially secure a parliamentary majority by partnering with either the left-leaning Progressives or the nationalist National Alliance. The election, which involved 14 parties contesting 100 seats via a proportional system, was shaped by concerns regarding national security and rising living costs. While most parties support high military spending and aid to Kyiv, the Sovereign Power party opposed military aid to Ukraine and increased defense spending, appearing set to finish third. An exit poll placed the populist Latvia First party in second place with 11.3%, nearly double its 2022 share. Both populist parties were noted as benefiting from shifts in voting patterns among Latvia's ethnic Russian-speaking minority.

pages.text: More than 1,200 students in Colorado have earned a climate literacy seal, a statewide initiative that combines climate-focused coursework with community service. cards.headline: Syrian Muslim Brotherhood holds second Shura Council meeting since fall of Assad regime

pages.text: The Syrian Muslim Brotherhood announced on September 27, 2026, that it held a Shura Council meeting, marking the second such meeting since the fall of the Assad regime. According to Syria Direct, the group is currently weighing its political future amid internal divisions and regional pressure as Syria undergoes a transition that leaves the status of political parties uncertain. In a statement, the group applauded the convening of the Syrian parliament and emphasized its importance for establishing organized political pluralism. Abdulrahman Alhaj, a specialist on Islamist groups, noted that the group's recent statement regarding partnering with national forces to rebuild the country indicates a preparation to participate in elections. However, as of October 2, 2026, the group faces external pressure to disband and continues to navigate internal challenges. The legal standing of political parties in Syria remains unsettled; while a 2025 announcement by al-Sharaa dissolved the Baath Party and parties affiliated with the National Progressive Front, a subsequent Constitutional Declaration stated that political participation and party formation will be governed by a new law that has not yet been drafted. Additionally, newly adopted procedures for parliament's work will ban political blocs and parties within the legislative body.

Founded in 1945 as an offshoot of the Egyptian Islamist movement, the Syrian Muslim Brotherhood was banned in 1980 by President Hafez al-Assad in response to growing Islamist militancy, which made membership in the group a capital offense. Following an attempted armed rebellion by an offshoot of the organization in 1982, the Syrian regime responded with the Hama massacre, resulting in the arrest or death of tens of thousands of civilians and Brotherhood supporters and driving the group into exile.

cards.headline: President Mahama proposes routes to South America and Caribbean for Ghana’s planned national airline

pages.text: President John Mahama has indicated that Ghana’s proposed national airline may explore routes to South America and the Caribbean to facilitate trade, tourism, investment, and people-to-people exchanges. During bilateral talks with Suriname’s President Jennifer Geerlings-Simons in New York on September 23, 2026, on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly, President Mahama suggested that connectivity with these regions could form part of the carrier's future route network. This follows an August visit to Jamaica, where the Presidency announced on August 3, 2026, that President Mahama and Jamaican Prime Minister Andrew Holness agreed to accelerate work on a Bilateral Air Services Agreement to facilitate direct flights between Accra and Montego Bay once concluded.

The proposed expansion has raised questions regarding whether available traffic data and the size of the potential passenger market support such routes. According to the Ghana Civil Aviation Authority’s 2025 international aviation statistics, Ghana recorded 2,539,034 international passenger movements that year, consisting of 1,238,220 arrivals and 1,300,814 departures. These plans come as Ghana confronts drug-trafficking cases. The 2026 World Drug Report identifies Colombia, Peru, and Brazil as main departure countries for cocaine shipments recorded between 2020 and 2024, noting that Brazil is also featured in trafficking routes to Africa and Europe.

cards.headline: Putin signs decree increasing authorized size of Russian Armed Forces to 2.44 million

pages.text: Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree on Tuesday increasing the authorized strength of the Russian Armed Forces to 2,441,630 personnel, which includes 1,550,500 service members, according to SANA English. The decree, which took effect upon signing, was published on Russia’s official legal information portal. The order instructs the Russian government to allocate necessary federal budget funding to the Defense Ministry to implement the provisions. This increase is linked to the creation of military construction units.

The new decree repeals Decree No. 419, which was issued on June 12 and previously set the authorized strength of the armed forces. This follows a previous increase in July that brought the total authorized strength to 2.426 million personnel, including 1.535 million service members.

cards.headline: Toronto mayoral candidates clash over use of AI in campaigns

pages.text: Toronto mayoral candidate Brad Bradford is defending his campaign's use of an artificial intelligence app following criticism from other candidates. According to CBC Toronto, the controversy arose after a National Observer report alleged that Bradford's campaign uses an AI app to provide online talking points to supporters. That report also alleged the app rewards users for sharing phone contacts with the campaign and posting social media comments. On September 28, 2026, Bradford denied that users receive any rewards, such as facetime, for posting AI-generated messages. His team stated to CBC News that the app's messaging and suggested comment features are intended to help supporters share their views with their networks. Bradford compared the use of the app to the campaign app used by Olivia Chow, stating the goal is to connect with voters. While technology experts noted that AI could serve as an equalizer for under-resourced teams, they stated it is no substitute for the human element of traditional voter persuasion.

cards.headline: Estonia attributes August arson attack on drone manufacturer to Russian sabotage

pages.text: Estonia has stated that an August 15 arson attack on a building in Tallinn used by Milrem Robotics was an act of sabotage commissioned by the special services of the Russian Federation. The manufacturer produces unmanned ground vehicles used in Ukraine. Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said on Tuesday that authorities have concluded with certainty that the attack was part of a broader campaign across Europe intended to intimidate Estonia and weaken support for Ukraine. Following the announcement, Tsahkna stated that Russia’s chargé d’affaires in Tallinn was being summoned to his ministry and described the attacks as “absolutely unacceptable.” An Estonian national security agency reported that two Latvian suspects were detained in Latvia on August 17, followed by a third suspect on August 18. All three individuals were subsequently handed over to Estonia. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov rejected the allegations, calling them “unfounded, ill-considered, absolutely not reflecting the reality, not containing any substantiation whatsoever,” and stated that Russia would not take the statements seriously. European and NATO leaders, including NATO chief Mark Rutte, expressed support for Estonia and Ukraine, with Rutte stating that Russia is attempting to weaken resolve and stop support for Ukraine. Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal stated the country's response would involve stronger domestic security, more support for Ukraine, and greater pressure on Russia.

cards.headline: Japan removes 16 Syrian entities from asset-freezing sanctions list

pages.text: Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced on Tuesday that it has removed 16 Syrian entities from its list of organizations subject to asset-freezing and other sanctions. The decision, which took effect through a Foreign Ministry notice, follows changes in the situation in Syria and Tokyo's consideration of bilateral relations with Damascus. Japan has maintained asset-freezing and other measures against Bashar al-Assad, as well as individuals and entities linked to his government, since 2011. Following the collapse of the Assad regime in December 2024, Japan partially eased these measures in May 2025, aligning with steps taken by other major countries. According to the Ministry, the latest decision was based on a Cabinet understanding regarding the partial lifting of sanctions and reflects subsequent developments in Syria.

The 16 entities included in the lifting of measures are Syriatel, the Military Housing Establishment, Real Estate Bank, the Political Security Directorate, Commercial Bank of Syria, Syrian Lebanese Commercial Bank, Syria Trading Oil Company (Sytrol), General Petroleum Corporation, Syrian Petroleum Company, and the Syrian Company for Oil Transport. Also removed from the list are the General Organization of Radio and TV, Syria International Islamic Bank, the Ministries of Defense and Interior, the Cotton Marketing Organization, and Mahrukat Company, which manages the storage and distribution of petroleum products. The Foreign Ministry stated that the broader sanctions regime will not be fully removed; asset-freezing and related measures will remain in place against 59 individuals and 15 entities.

cards.headline: Ontario woman acquitted in 2002 infant death following new medical evidence

pages.text: Jennifer Gaskin was acquitted on Tuesday in the death of her infant son, Joeseph, after more than two decades of being labeled as his killer. Gaskin was originally convicted in 2002 after two medical experts testified that her 2 1/2-month-old son had died as a result of shaken baby syndrome. Joeseph was a premature baby who had spent the first two months of his life in a hospital. Following an Ontario provincial examination of shaken-baby cases occurring between the mid-1980s and mid-2000s, Gaskin's legal team retained three additional experts to review the case file. During court proceedings on Tuesday, these three experts stated that while they could not rule out the possibility of an inflicted injury, Joeseph could also have died from sudden infant death syndrome. The Crown informed the Appeal Court that the original expert evidence supporting the conviction had been 'wholly undermined and placed in grave doubt,' and requested that the new findings be admitted as fresh evidence to allow for Gaskin's acquittal.

cards.headline: KNUST and UNCDF host EU Ambassador to advance skills development initiative

pages.text: The Career Services Centre of the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) has reaffirmed its commitment to providing students with industry-ready skills through collaborations with the United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) and the European Union. The European Union Ambassador to Ghana, H.E. Rune Skinnebach, and a delegation visited the university’s Career Services Centre to focus on youth empowerment, employability, digital skills training, and academic-industry collaboration. The visit aimed to strengthen cooperation among KNUST, the European Union, and UNCDF to advance innovation, entrepreneurship, and youth employability in Ghana and beyond. Ambassador Skinnebach described KNUST as a leading force in higher education and innovation within Ghana and West Africa, noting the European Union's commitment to supporting young people through initiatives such as Erasmus+ and European Horizons.

Mrs. Selina Angmor Doe, Director of the KNUST Career Services Centre, stated that the university was selected last year as an implementer of the European Union’s Skills Project in collaboration with UNCDF. According to Doe, the partnership has resulted in the reconstruction of the Centre’s website to include a job board for employers to upload opportunities for students and graduates. Additionally, the partnership has enabled the training of over 3,000 students in IT skills intended to increase international competitiveness.
